objects.description: Singleton-like utility class providing static APIs to discover OpenCL platforms/devices and to obtain process-wide default device, context, and command queue. It caches the first-resolved defaults (optionally thread-safe) and allows selecting via environment variables. No instances are intended; all methods are static.
This header file is a meta-header that only includes other Boost.Compute functional headers. It does not define any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes itself.

No custom types are defined in this header. It is a meta-header that only includes other headers (local_buffer.hpp and svm_ptr.hpp). Types referenced or defined in those included headers are out of scope per the instructions.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::default_device
functions.description: Returns the system-wide default OpenCL compute device. Selection is done once on first call using heuristics and may be influenced by environment variables (BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_DEVICE, BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_DEVICE_TYPE, BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_PLATFORM, BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_VENDOR, BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_ENFORCE). Subsequent calls return the same device. Throws if no device can be found under the selection rules.
requirements: The host system must have at least one OpenCL-capable device available; otherwise no_device_found may be thrown.
If BOOST_COMPUTE_DEFAULT_ENFORCE is set to "1" and any of the related default-selection environment variables is set but no match is found, the function throws no_device_found.
Callers should not assume the device changes across calls; the selected device is cached after the first call.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::find_device
functions.description: Searches all OpenCL devices on the system and returns the one whose name matches exactly the provided string. Useful for selecting a specific GPU/CPU by its reported cl_device_name.
requirements: The name argument must exactly match device.name() of an available device to succeed.
If no device with the given name exists, the function throws boost::compute::no_device_found.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::devices
functions.description: Enumerates and returns all OpenCL devices across all detected OpenCL platforms on the system. Intended for iteration and manual selection.
requirements: OpenCL platforms must be discoverable via clGetPlatformIDs; otherwise the returned vector may be empty.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::device_count
functions.description: Returns the total number of OpenCL devices available across all platforms on the system. A convenience count helper for quick checks.
requirements: None beyond being able to enumerate platforms and their devices.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::default_context
functions.description: Returns the system-wide default OpenCL context, created on first use for the default_device(). Subsequent calls return the same context object.
requirements: A default device must be obtainable (default_device()); otherwise default_device() may throw no_device_found and context creation would not proceed.
Context is created once and reused; callers should not assume it changes across calls.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::default_queue
functions.description: Returns a reference to the system-wide default OpenCL command queue. On first use, if a non-empty user_queue is provided, the system’s default device and context are initialized to match it. If a provided user_queue’s device/context do not match already-initialized defaults, a set_default_queue_error is thrown. Subsequent calls return the same queue.
requirements: If providing a user_queue, it must be a valid (non-null) queue whose device and context are consistent with each other.

If a user_queue is provided on the first call, it will define the defaults; if it is provided on any later call after initialization, this is invalid and triggers an assertion (the API expects no user_queue after initialization).
If a user_queue is provided and its device/context do not match the defaults already set, the function throws set_default_queue_error.
If no user_queue is provided on first call, the function will create a queue for default_context() and default_device(); those must be creatable.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::finish
functions.description: Blocks until all previously enqueued operations on the default command queue complete. Equivalent to system::default_queue().finish().
requirements: Requires that the default command queue can be obtained or created; otherwise any underlying failures would surface from default_queue() or queue.finish().

functions.name: boost::compute::system::platforms
functions.description: Enumerates and returns all OpenCL platforms present on the system using clGetPlatformIDs. Useful for manual exploration and selection of devices by platform.
requirements: The OpenCL ICD/driver must be installed so clGetPlatformIDs can succeed. If no platforms are present, the returned vector will be empty.

functions.name: boost::compute::system::platform_count
functions.description: Returns the number of OpenCL platforms on the system using clGetPlatformIDs. Convenience helper for quick presence checks.
requirements: OpenCL runtime must be available for clGetPlatformIDs; otherwise count will be zero or the underlying call may fail depending on platform.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte string used as a device name. Any sequence of bytes/characters is accepted; no specific encoding, structure, or character class is required. The function compares it to device.name() for an exact match and may throw if no device with that exact name exists.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets an "arbitrary string" buffer consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# in the fuzzer stub for boost::compute::system::find_device(name).
# Goal: produce interesting, but valid, device-name-like strings to trigger both
# matching and non-matching behaviors across diverse environments.
# Since we cannot query the actual system devices here, we synthesize a variety of
# realistic and edge-case names, including common GPU/CPU vendor/model patterns,
# exact whitespace/UTF-8 cases, and random variants. The fuzzer harness will also
# sometimes replace our string with a real device name from the runtime.

# Upper bound per requirements
MAX_SIZE = 4096

COMMON_VENDOR_TOKENS = [
    "NVIDIA", "GeForce", "RTX", "Quadro", "Tesla",
    "AMD", "Radeon", "RX", "Vega", "Instinct",
    "Intel", "UHD Graphics", "Iris", "Xe",
    "Apple", "M1", "M2", "M3",
    "ARM", "Mali", "PowerVR", "Adreno",
    "Mesa", "llvmpipe", "softpipe",
    "OpenCL", "Compute", "Accelerator"
]

# Some plausible full device name patterns commonly seen via cl_device_name
TEMPLATE_NAMES = [
    "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080",
    "NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti",
    "NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB",
    "NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB",
    "AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT",
    "AMD Radeon VII",
    "AMD Radeon Pro W6800",
    "Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630",
    "Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics",
    "Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1185G7 CPU @ 3.00GHz",
    "Apple M1",
    "Apple M2 Max",
    "QUALCOMM Adreno 650",
    "ARM Mali-G78",
    "Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (CML GT2)",
    "llvmpipe (LLVM 13.0.1, 256 bits)",
    "Portable Computing Language"
]

UNICODE_VARIANTS = [
    "ＧｅＦｏｒｃｅ ＲＴＸ ３０８０",   # fullwidth
    "ГеФорс РТХ 3080",                 # Cyrillic lookalikes
    "GeForce RTX 3080™",               # trademark symbol
    "Radeon RX 6800 — Navi",           # em dash
    "Iris Xe – Integrated",            # en dash
    "A100•SXM4•80GB",                  # bullet separators
]

WHITESPACE_EDGE = [
    "",  # empty string
    " ",
    "\t",
    "\n",
    "\r\n",
    "\x00",  # embedded NUL
    "  NVIDIA   GeForce   RTX   3090  ",
    "NVIDIA\tGeForce\nRTX\r3090",
]

# Construct a library of interesting names to pick from
BASE_CASES: List[str] = TEMPLATE_NAMES + UNICODE_VARIANTS + WHITESPACE_EDGE

# Some crafted strings to probe exact-match behaviors and boundary conditions
def boundary_names() -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Very long name near the limit (but keep overall buffer small)
    long_core = "GeForce" * 200  # 7*200=1400 chars
    names.append(long_core[:2000])
    # Mixed case variants
    names.append("nvidia geforce rtx 3080")
    names.append("Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080")
    names.append("NVIDIA GEFORCE RTX 3080")
    # Trailing/leading spaces and tabs
    names.append("\tIntel(R) UHD Graphics 630\t")
    names.append(" AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT ")
    # Names containing nulls and control chars
    names.append("Radeon\x00RX 6800")
    names.append("Intel\x1fXe\x7fGraphics")
    # Simple CPU strings that sometimes appear as OpenCL CPU devices
    names.append("Intel(R) CPU")
    names.append("AMD CPU")
    return names

# Random realistic device name assembly
def random_device_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    vendor = rng.choice(["NVIDIA", "AMD", "Intel", "Apple", "QUALCOMM", "ARM", "Mesa"])    
    if vendor == "NVIDIA":
        series = rng.choice(["GeForce", "Quadro", "Tesla", "A100", "H100"])    
        if series in ("A100", "H100"):
            suffix = rng.choice(["-SXM4-80GB", "-PCIe-40GB", "-SXM-80GB"])
            name = f"NVIDIA {series}{suffix}"
        else:
            family = rng.choice(["GTX", "RTX"]) if series == "GeForce" else series
            number = rng.choice(["1060", "1080 Ti", "2060", "2080 Ti", "3060", "3080", "3090", "4070 Ti", "4090"])
            name = f"NVIDIA GeForce {family} {number}" if series == "GeForce" else f"NVIDIA {series} {number}"
    elif vendor == "AMD":
        family = rng.choice(["Radeon", "Radeon Pro", "Instinct"])        
        if family == "Instinct":
            model = rng.choice(["MI50", "MI100", "MI210", "MI250X"])    
        else:
            model = rng.choice(["RX 5700 XT", "RX 6800 XT", "RX 7900 XTX", "VII", "Vega 64"]) 
        name = f"AMD {family} {model}"
    elif vendor == "Intel":
        family = rng.choice(["UHD Graphics", "Iris Xe Graphics", "GPU", "CPU"]) 
        if family == "CPU":
            core = rng.choice(["i7-1185G7", "i9-12900K", "i5-8265U"]) 
            name = f"Intel(R) Core(TM) {core} CPU @ 3.00GHz"
        else:
            name = f"Intel(R) {family} {rng.choice(['510', '620', '630', '770'])}"
    elif vendor == "Apple":
        name = rng.choice(["Apple M1", "Apple M1 Pro", "Apple M2", "Apple M2 Max", "Apple M3"]) 
    elif vendor == "QUALCOMM":
        name = rng.choice(["QUALCOMM Adreno 650", "QUALCOMM Adreno 740"]) 
    elif vendor == "ARM":
        name = rng.choice(["ARM Mali-G76", "ARM Mali-G78", "ARM Mali-T860"]) 
    else:  # Mesa
        name = rng.choice([
            "llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.7, 256 bits)",
            "Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (CML GT2)",
        ])
    # Occasionally add parenthetical vendor/platform suffixes
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        name += rng.choice([" (OpenCL)", " (Experimental)", " (RadeonSI)", " (CUD A)".replace(" ", "")])
    return name

# Random unlikely-to-match junk (still valid string)
def random_unlikely(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(0, 256)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+()[]{}\t\n\r\x00\x1f\x7f"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    # Occasionally ensure it contains vendor tokens to be close-but-not-exact
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        token = rng.choice(COMMON_VENDOR_TOKENS)
        insert_at = rng.randrange(0, len(s) + 1)
        s = s[:insert_at] + token + s[insert_at:]
    return s

# Main generator
# Returns bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumption. The fuzzer may also request
# other primitive params independently; we only control the string buffer here.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Assemble a pool of candidates
    candidates: List[str] = []
    candidates.extend(BASE_CASES)
    candidates.extend(boundary_names())

    # Generate several random realistic names
    for _ in range(10):
        candidates.append(random_device_like(rng))

    # Generate a few unlikely randoms
    for _ in range(6):
        candidates.append(random_unlikely(rng))

    # Add combinations to probe exact-match nuances
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Case variations
        base = rng.choice(TEMPLATE_NAMES)
        candidates.append(base.lower())
        candidates.append(base.upper())
        candidates.append(base + " ")
        candidates.append(" " + base)
        candidates.append("\t" + base + "\t")

    # Choose a final candidate
    s = rng.choice(candidates)

    # Enforce max size and return bytes (UTF-8 with surrogate escapes to preserve all code points)
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')[:MAX_SIZE]
    return b
